title: Israel-Hamas truce collapses and fighting resumes in Gaza
body:
On 1 December 2023, Israel resumed airstrikes in Gaza after a week-long truce with Hamas broke down. The first strikes hit Rafah shortly after 7 a.m. local time, according to NPR. The Israeli military said Hamas had violated the operational pause and fired toward Israeli territory. Hamas blamed Israel for rejecting terms to free more hostages and extend the truce.

During the pause, which began on 24 November and was extended twice, Hamas released more than 100 hostages, most of them Israelis, and Israel freed 240 Palestinians from its prisons. On the final day, Hamas released only eight captives, short of the 10 per day agreed under the extension terms. Qatar, a mediator, said talks to restore the truce were continuing.

Gaza's health ministry said more than 30 Palestinians were killed in the first hours of renewed fighting and reported at least 13,300 killed in the war overall, according to NPR. Reuters later reported that health officials put the toll for the day at 184 killed and at least 589 wounded. Israel said Hamas's 7 October attack killed about 1,200 people and that about 240 hostages were seized. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he regretted the resumption of military operations.
